summary: The Commonwealth PhD Scholarships for least developed countries and vulnerable states are UK government scholarships run by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC) and funded by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office. They support full-time doctoral study at approved UK universities for people from 17 listed Commonwealth countries who could not otherwise afford to study in the UK. The award covers tuition fees, a monthly stipend, return airfare and other grants for 36 months. Candidates do not apply to the CSC directly: they apply to a nominating organisation in their country and also complete the CSC online form.
eligibility_notes:
Nationality and residence: you must be a citizen of an eligible Commonwealth country, or hold refugee status granted by one, or be a British Protected Person, and you must be permanently resident in an eligible country. The 17 eligible countries are Bangladesh, The Gambia, Kiribati, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Nigeria, Pakistan, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Togo, Tuvalu, Uganda and Zambia.

Academic: you must be available to start UK study by the start of the September 2027 academic year. By September 2027 you must hold a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) honours, or a lower second-class degree plus a relevant postgraduate qualification (usually a Master's). You must not be registered for a PhD, or an MPhil leading to a PhD, before September/October 2026. Disabled applicants who show potential to contribute to international development but lack a 2:1 may be considered for a contextualised nomination through the Commonwealth Disabled People's Forum nominator.

Financial: you must be unable to afford UK study without the scholarship.

Documents: you must supply all required supporting documents in the required format. Applications with missing transcripts or missing pages are ineligible.

Not eligible: employees, former employees (within three years of leaving, for former staff of the listed bodies) and relatives of UK Government employees; staff of the Association of Commonwealth Universities or the British Council; CSC Commissioners, former Commissioners and their relatives. Anyone convicted of bribery under the UK Bribery Act 2010 may be banned from reapplying for up to five years.

Other rules: the study must fit one of the six CSC development themes. Four-year PhDs are not supported. There is no support for the overseas fossil fuel energy sector (extraction, production, transport, refining and marketing of crude oil, natural gas or thermal coal, and fossil-fuel power plants). Scholars must commit to return home after the award, and switching to a graduate or other visa to stay in the UK is not permitted. Other awards covering the same costs cannot be held at the same time. The CSC does not require an English test to apply; universities set their own English requirements.
age_experience_notes: There is no age limit, but applicants should check any leave restrictions set by their employer. Work experience is not required (general FAQ). You must not have been registered for a PhD, or an MPhil leading to a PhD, before September/October 2026.
funding_summary: The award is made for 36 months of full-time study for one doctoral degree. It covers tuition fees in full, a monthly stipend (GBP 1,712, or GBP 2,000 at London-area universities), approved return airfare, a study travel grant and, where approved, one fieldwork airfare. Family allowances are only a partial contribution. Dependants' airfares and journeys made before the award is confirmed are not covered.
programmes_note: The CSC makes these awards under six development themes: Science and technology for development; Improving population health, health systems and capacity; Promoting innovation and entrepreneurship; Strengthening peace, security and governance; Strengthening resilience and response to crises; and Access, inclusion and opportunity. The study must be linked to one of the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals. The programme list is not fixed: you propose your own doctoral research topic and name which qualification you are applying for.
institutions_note: Awards are placed only at UK universities that have signed an agreement with the CSC, under which the university pays 20% of the overseas tuition fee and any fees above the CSC fee cap. 89 universities are on the CSC list, from Aberystwyth University to York St John University (for example Cambridge, Oxford, UCL, Imperial, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Leeds, Manchester). Applicants list three universities and supervisors in order of preference with reasons; the CSC makes the final placement decision and may overrule preferences. Admission applications should be started before the scholarship application, and admission is needed for the scholarship to proceed.

summary.detail: Full-time PhD study at an approved UK university for 36 months. One degree only; no concurrent courses. Four-year PhDs are not supported. A signed supporting statement from a proposed UK supervisor is required. The research must fit one of the six CSC development themes. The programme is taught and supervised in English at UK universities; no national English test is required to apply to the CSC.

benefits.limit_text: Full tuition fees, by agreement between the CSC and the university
benefits.conditions: Scholars pay no part of the fee. 36 months of full-time study, one degree only.

benefits.limit_text: GBP 1,712 per month, or GBP 2,000 per month at universities in the London metropolitan area
benefits.conditions: Paid monthly for the period of the award; stated as the current rates.

benefits.limit_text: Approved return airfare from the home country to the UK and back at the end of the award
benefits.conditions: Not covered: dependants' fares, and journeys made before the award is confirmed. The general FAQ says scholars must leave the UK within one month of the end of the award or programme, whichever is earlier, or may lose airfare and excess baggage entitlements.

benefits.limit_text: Study travel grant towards study-related travel within the UK or overseas; where approved, one economy-class return airfare to the fieldwork location; a paid airfare to the home country for a mid-term visit
benefits.conditions: The mid-term visit airfare is not paid if the scholar claims spouse or child allowances or has received a fieldwork return airfare.

benefits.limit_text: Spouse allowance GBP 313 per month (maximum nine months, spouse only); child allowance GBP 313 per month for the first child and GBP 154 per month for the second and third child under 16; single, widowed or divorced parent: GBP 622 per month for the first child and GBP 154 per month for the second and third child under 16
benefits.conditions: Only if family live together in the UK; other conditions apply, including where the spouse also holds a scholarship. These allowances are only a partial contribution and scholars must be able to support accompanying family.

benefits.limit_text: Disability support: a full needs assessment and eligibility review for additional financial support
benefits.conditions: Under the CSC disability support statement.
The general CSC FAQ says the CSC covers airfare, visa costs and a living allowance for UK study. Scholars must still meet UK Visas and Immigration rules, which the CSC does not control.

benefits.limit_text: Other awards covering the same costs
benefits.conditions: Cannot be held at the same time as this scholarship.

requirements.text: Proof of citizenship or refugee status: a copy of a valid passport (or national ID card) showing photo, date of birth and country of citizenship. Uploaded as PDF to the CSC online application system by the deadline.

Full transcripts of all higher education qualifications, including to-date transcripts for current courses, with certified translations if not in English. Missing transcripts or missing pages make the application ineligible. If to-date transcripts are not available, explain why. Applicants must obtain and upload their own transcripts; the CSC does not contact universities.

At least two signed references, uploaded as PDF, on institutional letterhead or sent by email clearly showing the sender's details, in the referee's own words. Referees should say how long and in what capacity they know you, your suitability and need for UK study of the subject, your analytical ability, original thought, motivation and perseverance, your strengths and weaknesses, and likely development impact at home. The form asks for three referees, one of them a current employer if applicable.

A signed supporting statement from a proposed UK supervisor at one of your named institutions, as PDF on letterhead or from a clearly identified email, in the supervisor's own words. It should confirm they are in principle willing to supervise you, have the facilities, how your study plan fits their department's expertise, how much of the plan they wrote, and that the programme can be completed within 36 months. Provide one from your first-choice university if possible; at least one named UK supervisor is required.

Development Impact statement in four parts: link to global, national and local development issues and to your chosen CSC theme; how you will apply new skills after the award; the expected development change (outcomes, timeframe, beneficiaries); and how impact could be measured and evidenced. Entered in the online form.

Detailed study plan and award objectives, plus a statement of which qualification you are applying for and three preferred universities and supervisors in order with reasons. The CSC advises precise methodology and sampling strategy, and that you write the plan yourself, not your intended supervisor.

Personal statement on your background, motivation for impact in your home country and any barriers overcome; career plans for the five years after the scholarship and long-term; voluntary activities and leadership. Also entered in the form: all undergraduate and postgraduate qualifications, up to 10 publications and prizes, and employment history and how it supports the UK programme.

Nomination: you apply to a national nominating agency or a selected NGO or charitable body; the CSC does not accept direct applications. Each nominator sets its own process, closing dates and extra criteria.
Health and Disability Form, submitted before the Confirmation of Award is issued.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only for candidates who are selected.

application_steps.title: Apply first to a nominating agency or NGO
application_steps.detail: The CSC does not take direct applications. You apply to a national nominating agency (the main route) or a selected NGO or charitable body. Each nominator has its own process, closing dates and extra criteria, so check with the nominator. Nominators send their candidates to the CSC in December 2026, and a nomination does not guarantee selection.

application_steps.title: Start doctoral admission applications and name three universities
application_steps.detail: Begin applying for admission to UK universities before the scholarship application, because admission is needed for the scholarship to proceed. List three universities and supervisors in order of preference with reasons. An offer letter is not needed at the time of applying to the CSC. Get a supporting statement from a proposed UK supervisor, ideally at your first choice.

application_steps.title: Complete the CSC online application and upload documents
application_steps.detail: Register on the CSC online application system (two-factor authentication at registration and every login). Prepare answers offline using the CSC template form and guidance, then paste them in. Upload passport or ID, transcripts, at least two references and the supervisor statement as PDFs by the deadline. Applications cannot be edited after submission, and documents sent by email or post are not accepted. There is no application fee. The 2027/28 deadline was 16:00 BST on Tuesday 20 October, and applications are now closed.

application_steps.title: CSC checks eligibility and scores complete applications
application_steps.detail: The CSC checks eligibility and considers only complete applications; incomplete ones are rejected. Applications are graded on three criteria: candidate merit (including academic record), quality of the research proposal, and potential impact on the development of the home country. The CSC favours research-for-development potential and partnerships between the UK and other Commonwealth countries. Personal circumstances are considered, and where all else is equal candidates from disadvantaged or marginalised backgrounds are chosen. There are no country quotas.

application_steps.title: Placement decision and outcome by email
application_steps.detail: The CSC makes the final placement decision and may overrule your university preferences, considering course suitability and value for money. It will not change a provisionally selected candidate's university or supervisor except in exceptional, unforeseeable circumstances. Outcomes are expected by July 2027 and arrive by email, so check junk and spam. Offers may be withdrawn if not answered within a set time.

application_steps.title: Health form, visa and start of study
application_steps.detail: Submit a Health and Disability Form before the Confirmation of Award. Start on the date in the Notification of Award, and meet UK student visa requirements, which are set by UK Visas and Immigration and not by the CSC. Sign an undertaking to return home as soon as possible after the award.

application_steps.title: Conditions while studying and leaving afterwards
application_steps.detail: Live in the UK throughout and get CSC approval before overseas travel. No paid work without prior CSC approval. Changes to the plan of study need CSC agreement. Follow the CSC Code of Conduct. The award can be ended for unsatisfactory conduct, progress or attendance, or if the university suspends or ends registration. Leave the UK within one month of the end of the award or programme, whichever is earlier. The CSC does not support staying under the Graduate route and gives no letters of support for post-award work or postdoctoral study in the UK.
